category: B · Computational roles and constraint enforcement

formulations.name: Data-misfit loss
formulations.category: B · Computational roles and constraint enforcement
formulations.meaning: Penalizes disagreement between predicted observables and measurements.
formulations.purpose: Couples empirical information to the physics-constrained state.
formulations.relation: It is optional for data-free forward problems and essential for many inverse problems.
formulations.symbols: \(\|\cdot\|_2\): Euclidean norm of the observed quantity.

formulations.name: Boundary-condition loss
formulations.category: B · Computational roles and constraint enforcement
formulations.meaning: Applies the boundary operator at sampled boundary points.
formulations.purpose: Softly restricts the neural solution to the admissible boundary behavior.
formulations.relation: Hard-constraint formulations replace this penalty by an exact trial-space construction.

formulations.name: Initial-condition loss
formulations.category: B · Computational roles and constraint enforcement
formulations.meaning: Penalizes mismatch with the initial state.
formulations.relation: It complements the interior dynamic residual unless the initial state is hard encoded.

formulations.name: Terminal-condition loss
formulations.category: B · Computational roles and constraint enforcement
formulations.meaning: Uses a final-time condition instead of, or in addition to, an initial condition.
formulations.relation: It shows that condition terms must follow the mathematical problem rather than a fixed PINN template.
formulations.symbols: \(u_T\): prescribed terminal state; \(N_T\): number of terminal points.

formulations.name: Interface state-continuity loss
formulations.category: B · Computational roles and constraint enforcement
formulations.meaning: Penalizes mismatch of a state that should remain continuous across an interface.
formulations.relation: It is a basic transmission condition in interface-aware and decomposed PINNs.
formulations.symbols: \(\theta^-,\theta^+\): parameters of networks on adjoining regions; \(N_\Gamma\): interface points.

formulations.name: Interface flux-continuity loss
formulations.category: B · Computational roles and constraint enforcement
formulations.meaning: Enforces continuity of normal flux or an analogous conserved interface quantity.
formulations.purpose: Adds conservation-aware communication between subdomains or materials.
formulations.relation: It complements state continuity when the governing physics requires flux transmission.

formulations.name: Forward PINN optimization
formulations.category: B · Computational roles and constraint enforcement
formulations.meaning: Optimizes the neural state while physical parameters are treated as known.
formulations.relation: It uses the same residual-and-constraint machinery as the inverse formulation.
formulations.symbols: \(\theta^\star\): trained network parameters; \(\boldsymbol{\lambda}\): fixed physical coefficients.

formulations.name: Joint inverse state-parameter optimization
formulations.category: B · Computational roles and constraint enforcement
formulations.meaning: Optimizes unknown physical parameters together with the neural state.
formulations.purpose: Unifies inverse inference and state reconstruction in one differentiable problem.
formulations.relation: The inverse formulation extends the forward problem by making selected physics parameters trainable.

formulations.name: Auxiliary parameter-field network
formulations.category: B · Computational roles and constraint enforcement
formulations.meaning: Represents an unknown spatially or temporally varying physical coefficient by a second trainable network.
formulations.purpose: Supports distributed inverse problems where a scalar parameter is insufficient.
formulations.relation: The governing residual couples the state network and coefficient network.

formulations.name: Data-assimilation objective
formulations.category: B · Computational roles and constraint enforcement
formulations.meaning: Combines sparse observations with governing relations and required conditions.
formulations.purpose: Expresses data assimilation as a physics-constrained optimization problem.
formulations.relation: It is structurally the same family as canonical PINN training but emphasizes partially observed states.
formulations.symbols: \(\mathcal{L}_{cond}\): collection of boundary, initial, interface, or other identifying conditions.

formulations.name: Hard-constrained value/Dirichlet trial function
formulations.category: B · Computational roles and constraint enforcement
formulations.meaning: Builds prescribed value constraints into the neural ansatz so they are satisfied identically on the constrained set \(\mathcal{C}\).
formulations.purpose: Removes exact Dirichlet/value constraints from competition inside a penalty loss.
formulations.relation: Derivative constraints such as general Neumann or Robin conditions require a derivative-aware hard construction rather than this value-only template.
formulations.symbols: \(A\): extension satisfying the prescribed value \(g\) on \(\mathcal{C}\); \(D\): vanishing distance/factor function; \(\mathcal{C}\): exactly constrained set.

formulations.name: Distance-function boundary construction
formulations.category: B · Computational roles and constraint enforcement
formulations.meaning: Uses a distance-like function to enforce a Dirichlet boundary exactly.
formulations.relation: It is a specialized instance of the general hard-constrained trial function.
formulations.symbols: \(d\): exact or approximate distance function; \(\partial\Omega_D\): Dirichlet boundary portion.

formulations.name: Augmented-Lagrangian physics constraint
formulations.category: B · Computational roles and constraint enforcement
formulations.meaning: Combines multiplier variables with quadratic penalties for constraints.
formulations.purpose: Offers a constrained-optimization alternative to fixed scalar loss weights.
formulations.relation: It treats physical requirements as constraints whose enforcement can be tightened iteratively.
formulations.symbols: \(C_j\): constraint residual; \(\eta_j\): Lagrange multiplier; \(\rho>0\): penalty parameter.

formulations.name: Equality, inequality, and KKT consistency
formulations.category: B · Computational roles and constraint enforcement
formulations.meaning: States the first-order KKT conditions: stationarity, primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity, under the usual differentiability and constraint-qualification assumptions.
formulations.purpose: Provides a complete constrained-optimization consistency statement when the physical problem itself contains equality or inequality restrictions.
formulations.relation: These conditions can be enforced through penalties, primal-dual updates, or specialized architectures; they are necessary first-order conditions under standard regularity assumptions, not an unconditional guarantee of optimality.
formulations.symbols: \(J\): objective; \(\boldsymbol{\eta}\): equality multipliers; \(\boldsymbol{\nu}\): nonnegative inequality multipliers; \(\odot\): componentwise product; \(\mathscr{L}\): Lagrangian.
